subject: history
title: The Cuban Missile Crisis 1962
welcome_lead: Thirteen days in October 1962 when nuclear war seemed inches away — relive the crisis that reshaped the Cold War.
meta_desc: History Cold War Adventure 3: Cuban Missile Crisis 1962, its causes, course and consequences.
final_note: You have stared into the abyss of 1962. The crisis prompted hotlines and arms control efforts that still resonate.

walkthroughs.body_html: After Castro's revolution (1959) and the failed Bay of Pigs operation, the United States imposed an embargo and continued covert action (Operation Mongoose). Khrushchev sought to redress the strategic missile gap, defend Cuba and gain bargaining leverage by secretly deploying nuclear missiles within striking distance of the US East Coast.

U-2 reconnaissance photographs of 14 October revealed missile sites. Kennedy convened EXCOMM and on 22 October announced a 'quarantine' of Cuba. Soviet ships turned back rather than challenge it. Behind the scenes, Robert Kennedy and Ambassador Dobrynin negotiated a settlement: Soviet withdrawal of missiles in exchange for a US no-invasion pledge and the secret withdrawal of Jupiter missiles from Turkey.

The crisis catalysed arms control: the Washington-Moscow hotline (1963), the Partial Test Ban Treaty (1963) and ultimately SALT and START agreements. It accelerated Khrushchev's fall (1964) and contributed to the doctrine of mutual assured destruction. Castro remained a thorn in US-Soviet relations.

mcqs.q: What was the theory of the four humours?
options: The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.
Medieval doctors knew about germs but used humours because they had no medicine.
Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Disease was caused by imbalance of blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile; treatment aimed to rebalance them via bloodletting, purging or diet. It dominated for nearly 2,000 years.

mcqs.q: Why did Henry VIII break with Rome?
options: Because the Pope excommunicated him for marrying Anne Boleyn.
Because he wanted England to become Protestant.
Jews were expelled because they refused to fight in the Crusades.
Primarily for an annulment from Catherine of Aragon, but also to seize Church wealth and assert royal supremacy — not for Protestant theological reasons.

mcqs.q: Why were Jews expelled from England in 1290?
options: Edward I expelled Jews after a century of restrictions and taxation had impoverished the community; antisemitism, debts owed to Jews, and political pressure all contributed.
Jews were expelled because they refused to fight in the Crusades.
The four humours were invented by Pasteur to explain bacteria.
Jews left England voluntarily because they were no longer welcome.
